payload.rationale: I estimate a 70% chance that the BLS September 2026 payroll increase reported in the October 2 release is strictly above 30,000; exactly 30,000 would not qualify. The supplied observations are June growth of 31,000, July growth of 21,000, and August growth of 162,000, averaging about 71,000, with August unemployment at 4.1%. This supports positive underlying hiring but also shows substantial variation near the threshold. The supplied FOMC projections of 2.3% annual GDP growth and 4.1% Q4 unemployment provide weaker, indirect support for continued expansion; they are forecasts, not September payroll observations. My transfer assumption is that September hiring remains modestly positive, with considerable month-to-month and measurement uncertainty. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that August was a temporary rebound and the much weaker June–July readings better represent the underlying trend. The strongest reason it could be too low is that August reflects a sustained improvement, leaving a 30,000 threshold comfortably below the current hiring pace.
limitations: Only three recent payroll readings are supplied; no September payroll observations, hiring indicators, or release consensus are available.
The probability is judgmental, not derived from a fitted or calibrated statistical model.
FOMC projections are uncertain and do not directly predict a monthly payroll change; payroll and unemployment statistics come from different surveys.
Supplied source excerpts cannot be independently verified here, and the full frozen settlement rules are not included.
